why: It sits in the graphs week but needs no traversal: each of the n(n-1)/2 vertex pairs independently has an edge or not, so the count is 2^(n(n-1)/2) mod 1e9+7, a fast modular exponentiation.
hints: How many unordered pairs of vertices are there, and how many choices does each pair have?
Pairs are independent, so the number of graphs is 2 raised to the number of pairs, n(n-1)/2.
Compute e = n*(n-1)//2 exactly (Python big ints) and return pow(2, e, 10**9 + 7). O(log e).
pitfalls: n = 1 has zero possible edges, so the answer is 1 (the empty graph).
n is up to 10^9, so the exponent is about 5*10^17: use modular exponentiation, never build 2^e directly.
In fixed-width languages n*(n-1) overflows 32 bits; reduce with care (the exponent may be taken mod 10^9+6 by Fermat).
